runs.interpretation: The bounded diagnostic instrumentation captured 43 complete provider stream lifecycles and no decoded-event idle timeout. Its longest response was 751,957 body bytes in 110.602 s, forming 3,465 complete SSE frames with zero incomplete bytes. The prior run-1 timeout at 120 s and 812,635 bytes was not reproduced, so no timeout-policy fix is justified yet. The task still failed independently: all 43 ACP tool starts and terminals were paired with no event gaps, but the model submitted exact job 133334e9-fbb0-4f36-9247-aff74a679794 and its first status 4.069 s later was completed; no running state or productive overlap was observed. The independent verifier rejected missing exact-ID running overlap and the two repair cycles. This attributes the horizon failure to task execution/model behavior, not ACP event loss or daemon/job status projection. The model ended after 595.398 s active work, below the 1,800 s requirement.

The agent completed all 36 provider requests, 36 ACP tool starts and 36 terminals without event gaps, idle timeouts, activity-stall termination, or request/disk cap exhaustion. It submitted exact job 011e4934-167e-44b3-8f4e-cffd8523166b, observed it running, then made seven more tool calls. The durable store shows that the job completed successfully after 7.743 seconds; no source file changed during that actual interval, and the agent never polled terminal state. The pending terminal notice remained durable for the next turn. The turn ended normally after 9.89 minutes with no repair cycles, no continuation evidence and hidden-verifier failure. This is a model/workload overlap failure, not ACP loss, scheduler failure, job execution failure or provider stream stall. The longest response completed normally after 129.436 seconds and 901,640 bytes in 4,127 complete SSE frames, showing the current stream decoder can handle a response beyond the 120-second threshold when it receives decoded events.

runs.interpretation: The diagnostic again showed all 42 provider requests and all 42 ACP tool starts/terminals observed without event gaps, provider idle timeout, or activity-stall termination. The background test job completed successfully in 5.656 seconds. The agent observed it running 2.980 seconds after submission, but its next tool started 13.816 seconds after that status; no source file changed during the job, and it never polled terminal state. The daemon persisted the completed state and a pending terminal notice. The model ended normally after 10.06 minutes; the hidden verifier could not complete because the final Cargo test command failed to compile/test the catalog-cli target (0 tests ran). This reproduces a workload/agent-sequencing gap: the task prompt does not state the 30-minute substantive-work requirement, and the prescribed background test is too short to support realistic downstream edits between model turns. It does not reproduce an ACP, scheduler, job-store, provider-stream, or disk-control failure.
